chunks.heading: How It Is
chunks.notes: The child-narrator recounts internalizing her parents' judgment of a homeless man, then catalogs poverty/hardship/hunger/overdose/pain in a stacked anaphoric list.

chunks.heading: How It Is
chunks.notes: The narrator turns from childhood belief to the aphoristic realization that "how it is" isn't how it has to be, closing on a rhetorical "So why?"

chunks.heading: Because that's just the way it is
chunks.notes: Catalogs society's whispered excuses and averted eyes at hunger/suffering, then lands on the aphorism that indifference is a choice, not a given.

chunks.heading: Because that's just the way it is
chunks.notes: Catalogs the wealthy's feasting, hoarding, and inherited excess turning to hollow ennui, closing on rhetorical questions about abundance that never nourishes.

chunks.heading: Because that's just the way it is
chunks.notes: A three-line closing aphorism reframing "how it is" as something "bought to be," landing the poem's final point.
